findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Make S4's run_live_matrix.py docstring reference the exact ADR number S3 (8257) lands, and add an AC assertion tying the two together (e.g., grep the consolidated-record filename rather than a literal number).
evidence: Child 8257 comment: 'the real number is the next free one at landing (ls docs/adr/.numbers | sort | tail -1, plus one). Substitute it in ... the runbook story's docstring edit.'
Child 6acd 0085 row hard-codes: 'ADR 0085 (archived into ADR 0121 §20); runbook infra/runbooks/reconciler-live-matrix.md'.
Child 6acd AC3: 'grep -n "ADR 0037" scripts/run_live_matrix.py is empty' — does not assert the replacement names the SAME number S3 used.
findings.finding: Ordering/dependency on ADR number resolution between S3 (8257) and S4 (6acd) is underspecified for the two children that both write the consolidated ADR number. S4 depends on S3 and both must agree on the final number; the plan's S4 cites '0121 §20' while S3's numbering comment treats the number as resolved only at landing ('ls docs/adr/.numbers | sort | tail -1, plus one'). If S4 lands with a hard-coded 0121 but S3's number shifts at landing, the runbook docstring cross-reference becomes a dangling ADR reference.
scenarios: S3 lands at a number other than 0121 (e.g., another epic claims 0121 first); S4's docstring then cites a non-existent ADR and check_docs_index / ADR cross-reference integrity is wrong, yet S4's AC (which only checks 'ADR 0037' is absent) still passes.
findings.suggested_fix: Tie S4's docstring edit to S3's resolved number via the filename/slug (which is fixed), or add a cross-child AC that greps the landed consolidated-record number into run_live_matrix.py.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Pin the section numbers S4 depends on (0085=§20, 0031=§10) in S3's acceptance criteria, or have S4 reference the ADR decision by title rather than section number.
evidence: Child 6acd 0085 row: 'ADR 0085 (archived into ADR 0121 §20)'; 0031 row references 'see S4' pointer and S3 Part D item 10 is 0031.

Child 8257 outline assigns 0085 to section 20 and 0031 to section 10, but AC only checks 'grep ... from ADR 0[0-9]{3} | sort -u | wc -l = 20' — it does NOT pin that 0085 is numbered 20 or 0031 is numbered 10.
Parent decomposition: 'S4 ... depends on S3'.
findings.finding: Dependency gap / conflicting cross-child assumption: child 6acd (S4, 0085 row) asserts ADR 0085 is 'archived into ADR 0121 §20', which is only true AFTER child 8257 (S3) runs. The plan declares S4 depends on S3, but S4 also edits 0031 and 0085's BODY procedures while S3 archives them; if S4's '0121 §20' section-number reference does not match the actual section S3 assigned, the runbook docstring cites a wrong section. S3's AC pins '20 headings' but not that 0085 is section 20 and 0031 is section 10 — the numbers S4 hard-codes.
scenarios: S3 reorders sections during drafting so 0085 is not exactly §20; S4's docstring '§20' then points at the wrong decision, and no child AC catches the mismatch.
findings.suggested_fix: Add to S3's AC an assertion that 0085's section is 20 and 0031's is 10 (the numbers S4 cites), or change S4 pointers to cite the decision title.

findings.finding: Scope overlap on ADR 0029, 0031, 0083, 0085, 0092 across children c159, 8257, and 6acd without a stated edit ordering for all of them. c159 rewrites 0083's status line and adds blockquotes to 0029/0092; 8257 then rewrites ALL 20 originals' status lines to 'Archived — consolidated into [ADR 0121]' and adds an Archived banner; 6acd moves procedures out of 0031 and 0085. The plan declares S3 depends on S2 (c159) and S4 depends on S3, but 0031 and 0085 are edited by BOTH S3 (status/banner + supersedes pointer) and S4 (procedure->pointer), and 0083/0092's c159 banners must survive S3's status rewrite. The children do not state whether S3's status-line rewrite preserves c159's just-added blockquotes or whether S4's procedure removal composes with S3's archived banner.
scenarios: S3 rewrites 0083's Status line that S2 just rewrote; if S3 preserves 'was: ...' it must capture S2's new text, otherwise the parens lose c159's Phase-2-landed status.
S3's 'pre-existing ## headings unchanged' check runs after S4 has added/removed sections in 0031/0085 if ordering slips, producing a spurious diff.
findings.suggested_fix: Add an explicit note in S3 that its 'was:' parenthetical copies whatever status/banner S2 left, and that S4 (depends on S3) edits only body procedure lines, not status/headings.
